errata: E1 network: the lab VM (192.168.56.210) sits behind a NAT router that forwards only 80, 5432 and an SSH port. From the internet only K1 (5432) and content on 80 (K6, K8, D3, D4) are reachable; K2-K5 are LAN-only. The key's 'reachable from the internet' wording for K2-K5 is false for this deployment. FOUND/PARTIAL graded on whether the tool names the issue. 'Outside exposures caught' denominator = 1 (K1 only among K1-K3).

E2 eyeline's scope file states --all-ports, which is false behind this NAT. eyeline therefore printed 'blocked'/'closed' for unforwarded ports, and its auth/KEV/blast-radius riders evaluate only ports it judged internet-reachable, so K2-K5 were not reported. Graded as printed. It also printed port 22 as 'closed' (SSH arrives on a forwarded high port) with no warning about the contradiction with its own SSH login.

E3 eyeline data-handling defect: raw/eyeline/report.json (lines 879-880) stores decoy D1's Redis --requirepass value verbatim. Counted as a data-handling defect in the eyeline column, not a false alarm. Value not reproduced here. Reported as being fixed.

E4 coding-agent protocol breach: despite a read-only prompt it performed active exploitation-type testing (a CVE test request to Grafana; opening the unauthenticated databases). Snapshots show no server change. Findings still graded. Request details not reproduced.
notes: Consistency rule applied: PARTIAL requires the item's port or service to appear inside an alert (FAIL/WARN/warning/suggestion/GAP/finding). Inventory or status lines (Lynis 'Redis (server) status FOUND') do not count. The same rule makes decoy ports inside an alert count as false alarms (vps-audit D1/D3/D5).
vps-audit's 3.5 rests on one indiscriminate line that lists every listening socket, including loopback-only ports; that same line produces its three false alarms.
Fix credit for K7: vps-audit's FAIL text gives an imperative remediation; eyeline's is a parenthetical comparison in a context section with no Fix block, so graded NONE.
Single run, one rater (this model), one lab, NAT deployment, no human testers. The grader did not build the lab or run the tools.
